title: Sparse Additive Models for Domain Generalization

problem.claim: Domain generalization seeks to improve performance on unseen domains under distributional shifts.

gap.claim: Feature representations from existing domain generalization methods often have weak interpretability.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces Sparse Additive Domain Generalization, which combines an additive structure with ℓq,1-norm regularization to support structured feature selection and interpretability.
The method has an additive kernel-based formulation and a neural additive model-based formulation.
The paper derives generalization error bounds for both realizations and establishes feature selection consistency under a rate-scaled regularization condition.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that empirical evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets validate the effectiveness of SpADG.
The authors report that SpADG is particularly robust in high-dimensional settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Domain generalization addresses performance on unseen domains under distributional shifts.
A prevalent approach learns domain-invariant feature representations.
Existing feature representations often have weak interpretability.
SpADG introduces sparse additive modeling with two realizations and theoretical guarantees.
Empirical evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets are reported to support effectiveness and robustness in high-dimensional settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not state the exact regularization condition or the form of the generalization error bounds.
The abstract does not describe the scope or limitations of the two realizations.
